app_name: OCR It – pull text out of un-copyable documents for your LLM

novelty.justification: The repo is only 3 days old, is not a fork, and offers a CLI wrapper for OCR despite existing tools with tens of thousands of stars, indicating an incremental approach.

system_requirements.justification: Install failed (install_success false) after 18 seconds and there is no PyPI package, showing poor accessibility.

current_relevance.justification: As a devtool-cli for extracting text to feed LLMs, it aligns with current OCR‑for‑LLM pipelines but targets a narrow niche.

differentiation.justification: With only 14 GitHub stars versus 76,137 for tesseract and 34,553 for ocrmypdf, and no unique benchmark advantage, it adds little beyond existing tools.

community.justification: The project has 14 stars, a single contributor, and was updated 2 days ago, indicating a very small community.

ease_of_use.justification: Zero of two tests passed (0/2) and the installation failed, providing a poor user experience.

ease_of_integration.justification: Only a CLI mode is available, no PyPI package, and no API surface, making integration difficult.

documentation.justification: No explicit data on wiki, GitHub pages, or topic tags was provided, so a neutral score is assigned.

maturity.justification: The repository is 3 days old, has 1 fork and 0 open issues, indicating an early‑stage project.

performance.justification: Benchmark timings (e.g., ocr_time_ms 0.50, tesseract_time_ms 10.41) are reported but lack comparative data, so a neutral score is given.

summary: A lightweight CLI tool that runs OCR on images/PDFs to provide text for LLM pipelines, but it is a thin wrapper over well‑established OCR engines.

github.description: Chrome extension: pin a screen region once, then hotkey your way through a paginated document. OCR runs 100% offline via bundled Tesseract.
